checks.finding: design.md `## Architecture` (lines 45-121) is a mermaid flowchart with ~25 named nodes and directional edges. (1) Top-level component boundaries: schemas (SCHEMA_PC/SCHEMA_PB), canonicalizer (CANON), sidecar generator/validator (GEN/VALIDATE), weakening detector (DETECT), publisher (PUBLISHER), guard (GUARD), handshake (HANDSHAKE), the five migrated entry points (SHIP/BOOT/INTERVIEWER/LITESPEC/LITEGATE) are all distinct nodes with described interactions, not a one-sentence naming list. (2) Integration with existing components: GUARD is labeled 'EXISTING, unchanged decision logic', PLUGIN-CONTRACTS.md/the five skill files are labeled 'existing, edited/human-applied (REQ-009)' and shown wired into the new mechanism via explicit edges (e.g. 'GUARD -->|full write-deny...| SIDE_PC', 'HANDSHAKE -->|--verify-response...| ENTRYPOINTS'). (3) Technology choices per layer: the adjacent `## Components` table (lines 122-158) has a Technology column for every node (Python; POSIX sh/PowerShell/Node; JSON Schema; YAML; JSON; Markdown); frontend-spec.md's Technology Stack table (a normative design.md refinement) covers the script-runtime layer in detail and states 'no browser/client UI' with reasoning; infra-spec.md states 'No new runtime deployment' with reasoning. All three required elements present with genuine interaction description, not names alone.

Built a directed graph from design.md's Architecture mermaid edges. Two graph-theoretic cycles exist: (a) ANCHOR -> DETECT -> GEN -> STAGE -> VALIDATE -> PUBLISHER -> ANCHOR, and (b) HANDSHAKE -> AGENT -> GUARD -> AGENT -> HANDSHAKE. Neither is a build/import-time structural dependency of the kind this check targets: (a) is an explicitly-documented, versioned publish-then-consume pipeline — each iteration reads the CURRENTLY-live approved-context anchor, computes a verdict, and only a LATER, separate `apply-human-copy` transaction supersedes that anchor for the NEXT iteration ('Weakening-detector approved-context anchor CLI contract', design.md lines 836-898; 'Human-copy publisher transactional bundle contract', lines 927-1016) — a standard state-versioning pattern, not a simultaneous mutual dependency preventing build order. (b) is an explicitly-documented sequential challenge/response protocol ('the script's role is reduced to challenge issuance ... and evidence verification only; the SKILL layer ... is responsible for instructing the agent to make the real tool-call attempt', Design Decisions, lines 1303-1325) with no ambiguity about ordering. Per reviewer-calibration.md's Finding Evidence Gate, a FAIL requires a concrete failure mode ('what implementation, verification, or downstream gate will break or become ambiguous'); neither cycle presents one — both are named, ordered, temporally-separated flows the design itself narrates step-by-step. No structural (build/import-order) circular dependency exists among the Components table entries.

`## API / Contract Plan` (design.md lines 439-1017) is extensive and not empty: it lists every new schema/CLI contract (project-context, provider-bindings, approval-sidecar, approver-registry schemas; canonicalization CLI; HMAC preimage/signing; policy-weakening-categories CLI; weakening-detector approved-context-anchor CLI; human-copy publisher transactional-bundle contract), each with method-equivalent flags, request/response (input/output) shapes, and exit-code taxonomies (satisfying bullets 1-2). Per reviewer-calibration.md's Finding Evidence Gate, no concrete downstream-misalignment failure mode is identifiable given this fact is stated verbatim in three other places in the same document and is fully test-covered; the check's explicit Major trigger ('Absent or empty API / Contract Plan section when requirements reference user-facing interactions') does not apply (section is neither absent nor empty, and this feature has no user-facing interactions).

`## Security Boundaries` (design.md lines 1486-1499) is present with a 9-row table (B1-B9). (1) Names every trust boundary crossed: content/approval separation, sidecar/registry write boundary, HMAC key custody, policy-weakening self-approval, track-selection fail-open, generator self-defense, hook-activation handshake integrity, human-copy publish integrity, publisher self-protection. (2) States the auth/authz mechanism at each boundary via the dedicated 'Auth/Authz Mechanism' column for every row. (3) Addresses PII/data classification: 'Data Classification' column reads 'internal' for every row; security-spec.md (normative refinement) states explicitly 'No PII, and no provider-specific detail, is stored by any artifact this Epic designs.' (4) Addresses OWASP Top 10 concerns: the 'Concern' column names STRIDE categories (Tampering, Elevation of Privilege, Spoofing, Repudiation, Broken Access Control) per boundary, and security-spec.md's dedicated `## OWASP Mapping` table explicitly covers Injection, Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Security Misconfiguration, Software and Data Integrity Failures, and Identification and Authentication Failures with concrete controls and AC references.
